name: Varrow Healthy Workplaces Act

source_sentences: Every employee accrues one hour of paid sick time for every 30 hours worked, from the first hour of work or from 1 January 2027 for existing employees, up to 40 hours accrued in a calendar year.
Paid sick time is paid at the employee's regular hourly rate.
Independent contractors, as defined by the state's existing classification test, and public employers are not covered.
Unused hours are not paid out at separation; an employee rehired within six months gets the balance back.
An employer whose policy provides at least 40 hours a year of paid time usable for the same purposes on the same conditions is deemed compliant.
Employers with fewer than six employees are exempt.
The Department of Labor Standards enforces the Act on complaint only, within two years of the violation; there are no routine audits.
A new appropriation of $3.4 million a year from the general fund pays for 25 investigators.

unclear.text: The carry-over rule is enforced from 1 January 2028.
readings: U1-a: hours accrued in 2027 and unused on 31 December 2027 must carry into 2028; only enforcement waits
U1-b: the carry-over rule applies only to hours accrued from 2028, so 2027 hours may lapse

unclear.text: Size is the "average number of employees during the previous calendar year".
readings: U2-a: every person on the payroll counts as one
U2-b: only employees who average 20 hours a week or more count

context: A survey by the state labor department found that about 62% of private employees already receive paid sick leave, or paid time off (PTO) that can be used for illness, and about 38% (about 1.0 million) do not.
Varrow's minimum wage is $13.50 an hour, indexed each year to consumer prices; about 9% of private employees earn at or near it.
